audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven chart rows disagreed with their own why-text, including the worst kind: win[6]/phases[6].side read 'Yorick' while whys[6] says 'Two-plus items flip to Cho'Gath'. Rows 0-2 read 'Yorick' while whys[0] calls level 1 'a neutral farm lane', whys[1] says level 2 'stays even' and whys[2] says 'Level 3 is even until your W is reliably up'. Row 4 read 'Skill' while whys[4] says level 6 favours Yorick.
audit.why: The packet levelChart (Skill, Skill, Skill, Yorick, Yorick, Yorick, Cho'Gath) matches all seven why lines exactly. It is also the only reading that makes sense of the matchup: Yorick owns the window between Dark Procession coming online and Feast stacks landing, and loses the very late game to stacked health and true damage.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 4 and 6 flipped across both layers as one atomic pair-matched group, with ratings brought along.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' (sequencingCues 0). Rupture is named as the tracked cooldown in eleven fields with no number attached, and Feral Scream is referenced as a silence risk with no range or cooldown.
audit.why: Rupture is a flat 6s at every rank with 950 range, which is short enough that dodging it buys you a defined six-second window rather than a vague opening. Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s in a 300-range cone. Feast is 80/70/60s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[1].d and early now carry those numbers and phrase them as windows to act inside.

audit.whatIsWrong: Carnivore was never mentioned anywhere on the page, and dontsFull[1].d under the heading 'Get silenced mid-cast' described a wasted cooldown instead of the silence.
audit.why: Carnivore restores health and mana on every unit Cho'Gath kills, scaling with his level — that is why a chip-and-poke early lane goes nowhere against him and why the first two levels read even rather than yours. Feral Scream's silence is what actually punishes you mid-cast, in a 300-range cone.
audit.corrected: early now names Carnivore as the reason your chip does not stick; dontsFull[1].d states Feral Scream's cooldown and cone range.

audit.why: missingInteractions rule 'resistances-invalidated' warns that Feast bypasses stacked resistances. whys[6] already says 'stacked Feast HP and true-damage execute ignore your ghoul chip', and report[8].t already builds Plated Steelcaps for the Vorpal Spikes autos rather than for Feast, which is the correct reason to buy them.
audit.corrected: No change needed — the page already tells you resistances are not the answer to Feast.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — Telegraphed. Dodge it and swarm. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — 6s flat, 950 range, telegraphed. Dodge it and you own the next six seconds. - Feral Scream: 11s silence in a 300 cone. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: Telegraphed. Dodge it and swarm. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Telegraphed knock-up, 6s flat. Dodge it, then commit inside that gap.

edits.before: Cho'Gath wastes Rupture (Knockup) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Rupture is 6s flat at 950 range — sidestep it, then walk him down.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Feral Scream silences in a 300 cone — commit from outside it.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are even farm — Cho pokes with Q rupture and Vorpal Spikes on the wave, and you just soak minions and respect the Q slow so his rupture can't land. Neither of you threatens a kill this early; last-hit cleanly with Q Last Rites and don't walk into rupture range for a cheap silence-free trade. Keep your E charge for when you actually commit at 3.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even farm — Cho pokes with Rupture (6s, 950 range) and Vorpal Spikes on the wave, and Carnivore heals him off every minion he kills, so chip alone will never stick. Neither of you threatens a kill this early; last-hit with Last Rites, stay outside Feral Scream's 300-range cone, and save Mourning Mist for the level-3 commit.
